title: Ecommerce Website Design: 20 Examples + Tips (2026)
summary: See 20 real ecommerce website design examples from Shopify brands, plus the elements, tips, and steps to design a store that builds trust and sells.
body_markdown:
Ecommerce website design refers to how an online store looks and works. A well-designed site makes it easy for shoppers to find products and complete a purchase.


Visitors form opinions quickly. A[peer-reviewed study](https://researchgate.net/publication/220208334_Attention_web_designers_You_have_50_milliseconds_to_make_a_good_first_impression_Behaviour_and_Information_Technology_252_115-126) found that people can judge a website’s visual appeal in as little as 50 milliseconds. A compelling first impression can encourage shoppers to keep browsing.


Whether you’re creating your first[online store](https://www.shopify.com/website/builder) or redesigning an existing one, this guide can help. Browse ecommerce website examples and learn how to select a platform. Use these design tips to make your store look its best.


## How to design an ecommerce website: Step-by-step


Designing an ecommerce website follows a repeatable sequence of decisions, from picking a platform to polishing checkout. These steps build on the design elements and tips covered below, laid out in the order most businesses tackle them.


1. **Select an**[ecommerce platform](https://www.shopify.com/blog/best-ecommerce-platforms) **.** Choose a platform that offers customizable templates and flexibility, so the site can be tailored to specific business needs rather than forced into a generic layout.
2. **Define the brand's**[visual identity](https://www.shopify.com/blog/visual-identity) **.** Settle on a color palette, pick no more than two fonts (one for headers, one for body text), and decide on a photography style before building out pages.
3. **Add trust-building elements.** Publish contact information, a clear return policy, secure payment options, and[customer reviews](https://www.shopify.com/blog/review-generation) so first-time visitors feel confident buying from an unfamiliar brand.
4. **Design product and**[lifestyle photography](https://www.shopify.com/blog/lifestyle-photography) **.** Shoot products on plain backgrounds from multiple angles, then add lifestyle images that show products in use to reinforce the brand aesthetic.
5. **Apply visual hierarchy and**[psychological design](https://www.shopify.com/blog/51875141-5-psychological-design-tactics-that-make-brains-tick-and-visitors-click) **.** Use color and layout strategically to draw attention to key elements like calls-to-action (CTAs), guiding the customer's eye through the page.
6. **Build for**[responsive](https://www.shopify.com/blog/responsive-web-design) **, mobile-friendly display.** Test the site personally across desktop, smartphone, and tablet to confirm the transactional flow works smoothly on every screen size.
7. **Structure clear site**[navigation](https://www.shopify.com/enterprise/blog/ecommerce-navigation) **.** Limit the top-level menu to a few direct labels, such as Shop, About Us, Bestsellers, and Contact Us, and move secondary links like Return Policy and Terms of Service to the footer.
8. **Simplify the overall**[layout](https://www.shopify.com/blog/blog-design) **.** Remove distractions like excessive banner ads, pop-ups, or competing colors that pull attention away from products and the path to purchase.
9. **Streamline the checkout process.** Add accelerated payment options such as[Shop Pay](https://shop.app/shop-pay) , Amazon Pay, PayPal, and Stripe so shoppers can complete a purchase quickly and securely.


## 5 elements of great ecommerce website design


- Building trust with customers
- Creating a visually compelling experience
- Focusing on responsive design across devices
- Designing clear site navigation
- Designing high-converting product pages


The best ecommerce websites make it easy for shoppers to find products and complete a purchase. These five elements improve the[user experience](https://www.shopify.com/blog/user-experience-design) from the first visit through checkout.


### 1. Building trust with customers


First-time visitors do not know if your business is legitimate or your products will meet expectations. Discounts may earn their attention, but shoppers need confidence before they buy.


[Stanford’s web credibility research](https://credibility.stanford.edu/guidelines/index.html) recommends making claims easy to verify and showing that a real organization stands behind the site. It also calls for professional design. Keep content up to date, fix broken links, and add the following[customer trust](https://www.shopify.com/blog/customer-trust-checklist) indicators as you[build your website](https://www.shopify.com/blog/start-online-store) .


#### Contact information


Add an email address to the contact page. Add a phone number and mailing address when available. Repeat key details in the footer.


Stanford also recommends making contact information easy to find. An[About page](https://www.shopify.com/blog/how-to-write-an-about-us-page) can identify the people behind the business.


#### A return policy


A[return policy](https://www.shopify.com/blog/return-policy) tells shoppers which items qualify for returns or exchanges and the window of time in which they have to act on those transactions. State who pays return shipping and how refunds are issued. Link the policy from product pages and the footer so customers can read it before buying.


#### Payment security


[Shopify Payments](https://www.shopify.com/payments) gives customers access to major credit cards and Shop Pay. You can also offer Apple Pay and Google Pay. Shopify uses PCI-compliant security technology to protect payment information.


Make security visible. Shopify provides free[TLS certificates](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/domains/managing-domains/secure-connections) , also called SSL certificates, for domains added to the platform. They publish the store over HTTPS, which displays a padlock beside its URL.


Show recognized payment badges near checkout and use trust seals only when they are current and verifiable.


#### Customer reviews and testimonials


Many ecommerce solutions let you import reviews posted to other sites. Reviews may include customer photos or social media posts. Display verified reviews near the relevant product information so shoppers can evaluate claims from previous customers.


### 2. Creating a visually compelling experience


Visual design determines what shoppers notice first. Use high-quality images across the site. Keep your[branding design](https://www.shopify.com/blog/branding-design) consistent from page to page. Place important information where shoppers can find it quickly.


Visual design also needs to be accessible.[WCAG 2.2 Level AA](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/contrast-minimum.html) sets a minimum color-contrast ratio of 4.5:1 for normal text. Large text needs a ratio of at least 3:1. Test foreground and background colors before publishing.


Use these design practices:


- **Photography:** Shoot[product photos](https://www.shopify.com/blog/12206313-the-ultimate-diy-guide-to-beautiful-product-photography) against a plain background and include multiple angles. Add lifestyle photos to show scale or use case.
- **Color:** Use[color](https://www.shopify.com/blog/color-psychology) to draw attention to the primary action. Never rely on color alone to communicate an error or status.
- **Fonts:** Choose one[typeface](https://www.shopify.com/blog/brand-typography) for headings and another for body copy. Keep the text large enough to read on small screens.
- **Psychological design and visual hierarchy:** Apply[psychological design](https://www.shopify.com/blog/51875141-5-psychological-design-tactics-that-make-brains-tick-and-visitors-click) principles with care. Use size to establish importance. Use placement to direct shoppers to key content.
- **Dynamic micro-animations:** Incorporate brief animations to confirm that an item has been added to the cart. Avoid motion that delays or distracts shoppers.


### 3. Focusing on responsive design across devices


[Dynamic Yield’s ecommerce benchmarks](https://marketing.dynamicyield.com/benchmarks/) found that mobile devices accounted for 75% of visits but converted at a 2.8% rate. Desktop generated 25% of visits and converted at 3.2%.


After making any major design changes, test a full purchase on a phone. Check menus and product images. Complete every form. Confirm that buttons are easy to tap.


### 4. Designing clear site navigation


Your[website navigation](https://www.shopify.com/blog/website-navigation) needs to help customers find products quickly. Good navigation can also improve search engine optimization ([SEO](https://www.shopify.com/blog/ecommerce-seo-beginners-guide) ) by giving search engines a logical site structure.


The[Nielsen Norman Group](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/menu-design/) recommends specific and familiar wording for menu labels. It also recommends front-loading key terms and making links large enough to tap. Use breadcrumbs or menu highlighting to tell shoppers where they are.


Limit the top-level menu to the categories shoppers use most. A basic menu might include:


- Shop
- About Us
- Bestsellers
- Contact Us


Stores with many categories can use a[mega menu](https://www.shopify.com/blog/mega-menu) or category landing pages. Avoid cascading menus with several levels. Place the return policy and terms of service in the footer. Add a contact link there as well.


### 5. Designing high-converting product pages


A product page needs to give shoppers enough information to make a purchase decision.[Baymard Institute usability testing](https://baymard.com/learn/ecommerce-cro) found that 56% of users began exploring product images immediately after reaching a product page.


High-resolution photos with zoom capability let shoppers inspect details, and additional angles give them a better view of the product. When size is difficult to judge online, an in-scale image shows shoppers how large the item is.


Shoppers also need to see the product name and price near the top of the page, with the add-to-cart button close by. The description can explain fit and use. Shipping details tell customers when the order will arrive, and the return policy explains what happens if the product does not work out.


## 20 best ecommerce website design examples (with key takeaways)


The best[website design](https://www.shopify.com/blog/best-website-design) examples are those that consider all the elements above for a clean, appealing, user-friendly design that communicates the brand and products clearly.

### 1. Thesus


Thesus


Sustainable shoe store[Thesus](https://thesusoutdoors.com/) masters trust-building by promising customers a super-easy online shopping experience.


The brand highlights their shipping and returns policy, plus an option to pay in installments if shoppers don't have the cash up front. Stellar customer support is highlighted right on the homepage with a handy size chart and returns links.


### 2. Welly


Welly


[Welly](https://www.getwelly.com/) positioned themselves as the fun first-aid brand with cute convenient packaging and kid-friendly bandage designs. That brand aesthetic is woven through their colorful website, complete with catchy copy and a clear CTA to “Shop Now.” The homepage is bold and dynamic without being cluttered.


### 3. Fred Jourdain


Fred Jourdain


Artists wanting to[sell their art online](https://www.shopify.com/blog/211990409-how-to-sell-art-online) could follow[Fred Jourdain](https://fredjourdain.com/) 's lead. The homepage lets the arts speak for itself, filling most of the page. You can also find interviews on the website and read more about how Fred creates his art. This content offers value to the customer while subtly nudging them to shop the artist's work.


### 4. MVMT


MVMT


[Mvmt](https://mvmt.com/) 's core brand value, "Style shouldn't break the bank," is reflected in their website design. The site presents sleek, sophisticated colors and styling that showcases watches, eyewear, and jewelry at affordable prices. Plus, it highlights collaborations with designers and provides a Last Chance section on their homepage so people can quickly check the fleeting designs.


### 5. Pure Cycles


Pure Cycles


[Pure Cycles](https://purecycles.com/) uses a simple layout that makes it clear why you should care about the brand, while showcasing their bestselling bikes.


Their product pages also work to give you an approximation of an in-person shopping experience while shopping online. You can see close-up pictures of specific parts, learn specs, and read other information you need to make an informed buying decision.


### 6. Verve Coffee Roasters


Verve Coffee Roasters


[Verve Coffee Roasters](https://vervecoffee.com/) uses customer reviews to build trust throughout their ecommerce website.


The online coffee retailer also uses evocative language paired with stylish photography to keep customers on the page, promising to be "classic and delicious" and serving lively descriptions, such as "the sweetness of golden marmalade."


### 7. Finn


Finn


[Finn](https://www.petfinn.com/) gives pet owners what they're looking for: big photos of happy dogs that inspire them to pamper their own. The brand's website also uses simple fonts, lots of contrast, and page hierarchy that directs visitors to Shop or Take Quiz. An interactive quiz helps customers feel more confident about their purchases.


### 8. Hardgraft


Hardgraft


[Hardgraft](https://hardgraft.com/) 's ecommerce store builds trust with buyers who want luxury goods and appreciate rugged, earthy aesthetics. Their brand mission and values are on display, telling visitors right away what they're about.


The brand's product pages are on point, with crisp, bold images that share important product features and value propositions. Plus, they offer safe, worldwide shipping, appealing to a broad international audience.


### 9. Topo Designs


Topo Designs


Outerwear shop[Topo Designs](https://topodesigns.com/) uses images that resonate with their target market—pics of Topo products in exciting travel destinations—while using unique backgrounds to stand out from other outerwear brands.


Another key website design best practice is how the brand communicates sales and incentivizes larger order values by offering free shipping above an order amount threshold.


### 10. Ketnipz


Ketnipz


[Ketnipz](https://ketnipz.com/) is an Instagram comic turned brand empire created by Harry Hambley. You can find Bean, the main character, on murals around the world, throughout social media, and even tattooed on the bodies of fans.


Ketnipz's website design reflects Bean's quirky personality, with bright colors, unique fonts, and seasonal updates to align product launches with upcoming holidays.


### 11. Chubbies


Chubbies


[Chubbies](https://chubbiesshorts.com/) ' website design evokes their brand values with captivating[product photography](https://www.shopify.com/blog/12206313-the-ultimate-diy-guide-to-beautiful-product-photography) and witty copy. The sidebar navigation, although different from most ecommerce website designs, presents a neat menu where shoppers can find their products faster and easier.


### 12. Kith


Kith


[Kith](https://kith.com/) 's homepage design grabs your attention the minute you land on it. The site feels clean, yet sparks interest, with links to treats and content such as lookbooks, films, journals, and more. Kith's catalog is big, but product categories are still presented in a way that lets you quickly explore and find what you're looking for.


### 13. Personal Fav


Personal Fav


[Personal Fav](https://personalfav.co/) appeals to their target audience by using trendy color palettes and fonts, with provocative imagery. While the site is bold and colorful, it's not busy. Clear top-level navigation gets customers quickly to the[brand's mission](https://www.shopify.com/blog/mission-statement) and product pages.


### 14. Satya Organic


Satya Organic


You can tell branding was a priority in skincare brand[Satya Organic](https://satya.ca/) 's ecommerce website design. Once you land on the homepage, you're met with earthy tones and signals that say, "If you're looking for plant-based goods, you're in the right place."


The footer of their website clearly lists the products' benefits and certifications like USDA Organic, cruelty-free, fragrance-free, and Indigenous-owned.


### 15. Beardbrand


Beardbrand


[Beardbrand](https://beardbrand.com/) takes a content-heavy approach to presenting their grooming products throughout their website design. Using a quiz, video of the founder, and educational blog posts, the site encourages you to stick around, engage with the brand, and buy.


### 16. Kylie Cosmetics


Kylie Cosmetics


As soon as you scroll the[Kylie Cosmetics](https://kyliecosmetics.com/) homepage, you see a picture of Kylie Jenner, a beauty icon for the brand’s target audience. Her endorsement immediately gives the site a huge trust and[credibility](https://www.shopify.com/blog/website-credibility) boost. Each product is also well displayed on a[plain background](https://www.shopify.com/blog/194970057-remove-background-product-photography-image) , and when you hover over an image, you can see a person using the product in action.


### 17. Tessemae’s


Tessemae's


To help build trust with their audience,[Tessemae's](https://www.tessemaes.com/) includes[user-generated content](https://www.shopify.com/blog/user-generated-content) (UGC) on their ecommerce site. This tells visitors that Tessemae's products are well loved among existing customers. Plus, the brand provides inspiration for the many ways their dressings and condiments can be used to create delicious meals, adding an extra incentive to buy.


### 18. Almond Surfboards


Almond Surfboards


[Almond Surfboards](https://almondsurfboards.com/) uses soft, warm tones throughout their online store to give the brand experience a stylish but beachy feel. The imagery is creative and unique, which makes it feel like a high-quality brand from the minute you land on the page.


In-context photography sells an aspirational lifestyle, suggesting even if you don't need a surfboard, you might be compelled to own a piece of the brand through T-shirts, accessories, wall art, and more.


### 19. Pura Vida Bracelets


Pura Vida Bracelets


To foster trust, jewelry retailer[Pura Vida Bracelets](https://puravidabracelets.com/) emphasizes the handmade and personalized aspects of their products. Their homepage includes product images featuring multiple models, while the headings highlight themes of friendship and community. Product reviews from thousands of customers scroll across the screen, above endorsements from target-audience-appropriate media outlets like Teen Vogue and Cosmopolitan.


### 20. Partake Foods


Partake Foods


If you love healthy, allergy-friendly treats, you'll love the website design for[Partake](https://partakefoods.com/) . The hero image immediately grabs attention with vibrant imagery, featuring a bowl overflowing with cookies, chocolate chunks, and colorful sprinkles.


Bold copy like "Partake in Daily Sweetness" and "Grab life by the cookies" gives shoppers a sense of the brand’s personality. Playful badges like "Better for you" and "Dang delicious for you" highlight flavor and nutrition. Dietary certifications and social proof across the site build instant trust with health-conscious shoppers.


## 7 best ecommerce website design tips


Your brand guidelines set the look of your online store. These seven tips can make the site easier to browse and buy from.


### 1. Keep it simple


Simple design keeps attention on your products. Remove banner ads and unnecessary pop-ups. Limit the number of colors on each page.


A good ecommerce platform offers[ecommerce website templates](https://www.shopify.com/blog/ecommerce-blog-post-templates) that provide a simple starting point.


### 2. Express your brand


People want to buy from brands they trust and recognize. Define what makes your business different from its competitors. Consistently use the same voice and visual style across your website.


### 3. Use the right platform


The best ecommerce platform is one that fits how you plan to sell products and operate your store.


Review these areas before committing to a platform:


- **Storefront:** Mobile-ready themes and flexible editing
- **Commerce:** Product and inventory management
- **Checkout:** Secure payments and local currencies
- **Operations:** Order-processing and shipping tools
- **Growth:** Built-in analytics with SEO controls and access to apps and additional sales channels
- **Performance:** Fast page loads and capacity for traffic spikes
- **Cost and support:** Affordable pricing with access to assistance


With Shopify, you can set up your store through its[website builder](https://www.shopify.com/website/builder) and use AI to generate a personalized theme. The[Shopify Theme Store](https://themes.shopify.com/) offers free and paid themes. You can filter themes by industry or catalog size. Paid themes can be previewed and customized in the theme editor before purchase.


### 4. Upload high-quality images


High-quality product images give shoppers a more accurate view of what they are buying.[Research suggests](https://www.blendnow.com/blog/do-better-product-photos-really-increase-sales) that multiple product photos can improve conversion rates compared with a single basic product image. A 360-degree view or 3D/AR content can give shoppers more detail.


Invest in good[product photography](https://www.shopify.com/blog/12206313-the-ultimate-diy-guide-to-beautiful-product-photography) . Use images from[free stock photo websites](https://www.shopify.com/blog/17156388-22-awesome-websites-with-stunning-free-stock-images) for editorial content and backgrounds.


### 5. Lead with professionalism


A polished website can earn trust from shoppers who have never encountered your business. Keep formatting consistent and check product information for errors. Make contact details easy to find before you[start an online store](https://www.shopify.com/blog/start-online-store) .


### 6. Leverage social proof


Place positive reviews on product pages where shoppers can use them to evaluate an item. Add user-generated content (UGC) that shows products in real settings. These posts give potential customers evidence from people who have already purchased.


### 7. Focus on checkout


A good-looking store can still lose the sale at checkout.[Baymard calculated](https://baymard.com/lists/cart-abandonment-rate) an average cart abandonment rate of 70.22% from 50 studies. Not every abandoned cart comes from checkout, but checkout problems can cost sales.


Keep checkout short and show the total cost before payment. Make forms easy to complete on a phone. Offer[Shop Pay](https://www.shopify.com/blog/shop-pay-checkout) and other accelerated payment options like PayPal.


Before making a permanent design change, use[Rollouts](https://www.shopify.com/test-and-launch) to schedule a theme change or A/B test a theme variant against your current theme. Shopify’s Rollouts tool measures conversion rate. It can automatically revert your store to the current theme when a scheduled campaign ends.

## Ecommerce website design FAQ


### What are the most important elements of ecommerce website design?


Good ecommerce design makes products easy to find and understand. It also works well on mobile and gives shoppers reasons to trust the business. A fast checkout completes the experience.


### How do you make an ecommerce website look trustworthy?


A trustworthy ecommerce site looks professional and provides accurate product information. Shoppers can easily find contact details and read the return policy before buying. HTTPS security and verified customer reviews provide additional evidence that the business is legitimate.


### How do you build an ecommerce website without a developer?


Hosted ecommerce platforms such as Shopify let you build a store with a visual editor and prebuilt themes. Shopify’s AI tools can also generate a personalized theme from a business description.


### What platform were these ecommerce website design examples built on?


The ecommerce website examples in this guide were built on Shopify. Stores can customize their storefronts through themes or custom code and use apps to add features when they need more functionality.


### How often should an ecommerce website be redesigned?


An ecommerce website doesn’t need a redesign on a fixed schedule. A redesign makes sense when the brand changes or the site is difficult to use. Regular design reviews can catch smaller problems that only need targeted updates.
